html:
A German school of art, design and architecture, founded by the architect Walter Gropius in Weimar in 1919 and closed under Nazi pressure in 1933. It set much of the look of modern design.

Its aim was to join art and craft with industry. Students learned in workshops, with metal, wood, weaving and print, and designed things meant for mass production: lamps, chairs, teapots, type and houses. Forms were plain and geometric, and decoration gave way to function.

Its teachers included painters such as Wassily Kandinsky and Paul Klee. The school moved to Dessau in 1925, into a glass and concrete building designed by Gropius, and in 1932 to Berlin under its last director, Ludwig Mies van der Rohe.

It was born with the Weimar Republic and died with it. The Nazis saw it as foreign and left wing and forced it to close. Its teachers and students scattered abroad, to the United States, Britain and Palestine, where many Bauhaus style buildings went up in Tel Aviv. That spread its ideas around the world.
sum: A German school of art, design and architecture, founded by the architect Walter Gropius in Weimar in 1919 and closed under Nazi pressure in 1933. It set much of the look of modern design.
